Generated ASN.1 C and the vendored C runtime compile as C17 (gnu17). gcc 15 defaults to C23, where bool/true/false are keywords and f() means f(void)

asn1c 18e56503 built with gcc 15.2 at -O2 segfaults in asn1f_fix_constr_ext: the TQ list macros access lists through pointers to distinct anonymous struct types (strict-aliasing UB), and 33 of the fork's own 130 compiler-output tests fail. Built with -fno-strict-aliasing (and -std=gnu17), 130/130 pass and the binary is reproducible (sha256 403a7ebb…). UBSan at -O0 also reports a signed __int128 shift in asn1p_integer.c (a constant for INTEGER max), which is benign

-fprefix=

_ is complete at 18e56503: two modules with identical type names, compiled with different prefixes, define 25 globals each with 0 unprefixed and 0 clashes, and none clash with the runtime. So there is no own type-prefixing tool; one prefix per protocol (RRC_, NGAP_, F1AP_, E1AP_, XNAP_)

encoding_constraints: at 18e56503 the generated descriptor initializers and the runtime's asn_encoding_constraints_t use the same ASN_DISABLE_*_SUPPORT guards, so no post-processing is needed. The layout depends on that macro set, so one forced-include header (src/codec/asn1/ksim_asn1_config.h: OER, BER, XER, RFILL off) goes into every translation unit, and generation uses the matching -no-gen-* flags. Generated C and the runtime are also built with -fno-strict-aliasing

JER is always generated. On the smoke module it adds 18 runtime files and about 25% object size, and no generated-code lines. It serves the oracle comparison and the ksim-codec JER dump, so the separate oracle preset is dropped (architecture.md section 10)

The runtime library is the skeleton subset asn1c lists in Makefile.am.libasncodec for our flags, compiled from the vendored copies (third_party/asn1c/runtime, unmodified). Each listed file must be byte-identical to the vendored one. The BER-only files (e.g. ANY_ber.c) are vendored but not built: they do not compile with BER disabled
